name: Fourth Year Vineyard Produce (Kerem Revay — Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of kerem revay: redemption procedures, borders of Jerusalem for transport, peret and defective clusters in fourth year, removal, and relation to maaser sheni laws. The existing kerem_revay entry is a stub; this covers the tractate's specific halakhic content.

name: Redemption Procedures for Maaser Sheni
notes: Detailed laws of redeeming maaser sheni: adding a fifth (chomesh), who may redeem, redemption at lower market price, evaluation by one or three, redemption by owner vs. others, conditional redemption, deceptive redemption techniques.

name: Adding a Fifth When Redeeming Maaser Sheni (Chomesh)
notes: Obligation to add one-fifth when redeeming one's own maaser sheni; who is obligated; applies to owner and one who received it as a gift; comparison with chomesh for redeeming other sacred items.

name: Biur Maaser Sheni (Removal of Second Tithe)
notes: The removal of maaser sheni on the eve of Pesach in the fourth and seventh years; timing; cooked dishes; what must be removed vs. what has already been treated as removed.

name: Viduy Maaser (Tithe Confession/Declaration)
notes: Detailed laws of the viduy maaser declaration (Deut. 26:13-15): text, timing (minhah of last festival day), who may recite it (Israelites, mamzerim; not converts or freed slaves per most opinions), disqualifying violations, the blessings invoked.

name: Eating Maaser Sheni in Jerusalem
notes: Laws governing consumption of maaser sheni specifically in Jerusalem: bringing produce in and taking it out, produce passing through Jerusalem, produce that became impure, eating after Temple destruction.

name: Maaser Sheni that Became Impure
notes: What happens when maaser sheni or items bought with maaser sheni money become ritually impure: redemption vs. burial, distinctions based on primary vs. secondary impurity, inside vs. outside Jerusalem.

name: Exchange and Currency Laws of Maaser Sheni
notes: Laws of exchanging maaser sheni money: silver to copper, silver to gold, exchanging in Jerusalem, minimum denominations, changing a sela, debates between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

name: Permissible Uses of Maaser Sheni (Food, Drink, Anointing)
notes: Maaser sheni may be used for eating, drinking, and anointing; prohibition on spicing oil; what may and may not be purchased with maaser sheni money; value improvements and proportional division.

name: Maaser Sheni: Sacred in Value vs. Sacred in Body
hebrew: קדושת דמים וקדושת הגוף במעשר שני
notes: Whether the sanctity of maaser sheni is a bodily sanctity or a monetary sanctity, affecting rules of redemption, becoming impure, items bought with maaser sheni money.

name: Marking Orlah and Fourth Year Vines
notes: The practice of marking orlah trees with potter's clay and fourth-year vines with clods of earth and graves with lime; timing of these markings (in the seventh year according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel).

name: Transferring Maaser Sheni Status When Produce is Distant
notes: Procedure for designating and transferring maaser sheni or tithing when one is physically distant from the produce, including the famous case of Rabban Gamliel on the ship; leasing the location to effect the transfer.

name: Enactments of Yochanan the High Priest
notes: The historical rabbinic enactments attributed to Yochanan the High Priest: abolition of the viduy maaser recitation, abolition of the 'wakers' (hammers in the Temple), and declaration that demai need not be examined in his day.

name: Found Objects with Markings of Sacred Status
notes: Laws of found money, vessels, or produce with inscriptions indicating korban, maaser, demai, tevel, or terumah: how to determine their status, presumptions applied, single-letter abbreviations used in times of danger.
